subtitle: Akbar’s Fire at Chittor and the Count in the Victor’s Own Book

panels.shot: epic wide of Chittorgarh fort looming over a smoky plain, Akbar in the foreground with matchlock raised, ghostly figures of Jaimal and Patta suggested in the stone
panels.action: Akbar_jaimal_and_patta stands in imperial armor on a smoky plain before the towering walls of Chittorgarh, matchlock resting in his hands, while faint spectral images of Jaimal_jaimal_and_patta and Patta_jaimal_and_patta seem carved into the fort’s ramparts.

dialogue.text: In 1568, at Chittorgarh’s broken walls, Akbar’s own chronicle speaks of jihad, jauhar, statues of valor—and a count of thirty thousand dead.

i18n.hi: १५६८ में, चित्तौड़ की टूटी दीवारों पर, खुद अकबर का इतिहास जिहाद, जौहर, वीरता की मूर्तियाँ—और तीस हज़ार मरे हुओं की गिनती लिखता है।

panels.shot: slow push-in from the sky over North India to the rugged hills of Mewar and the island city of Chittor
panels.action: A bird’s-eye view shows the green plains of Hindustan giving way to the rocky hills of Mewar, with the long-backed ridge of Chittorgarh fort rising like a stone ship above fields and the Berach river.

dialogue.text: By the late 1560s, the Mughal empire spread across North India, but Mewar still stood apart, its capital Chittor a long stone ridge holding the old pride of the Sisodia house.

i18n.hi: १५६० के आखिर तक मुग़ल सल्तनत उत्तर भारत में फैल चुकी थी, पर मेवाड़ अब भी अलग खड़ा था—उसकी राजधानी चित्तौड़, लम्बी पत्थर की पहाड़ी पर सिसोदियों की पुरानी शान।

panels.shot: medium wide inside Akbar’s camp-tent, maps spread, officers in turbans and armor around him
panels.action: Inside a rich but functional war tent, Akbar_jaimal_and_patta in his mid-twenties leans over a large cloth map marked with forts and routes, commanders around him listening as he gestures toward a stylized Chittor.

dialogue.text: Akbar, barely twenty-five, had taken Malwa and faced Gujarat; most Rajput houses had chosen alliance. But Mewar’s Rana Udai Singh refused submission, and Chittor became a frontier the emperor would not leave behind him.

i18n.hi: पच्चीस बरस का अकबर मलवा ले चुका था, गुजरात से भिड़ रहा था; ज़्यादातर राजपूत घराने साथ जुड़ गए थे। पर मेवाड़ के राणा उदय सिंह ने सिर झुकाने से इनकार किया, और चित्तौड़ वो सरहद बना जिसे बादशाह पीछे नहीं छोड़ सकता था।

panels.shot: close-up on Akbar’s determined face lit by lamp-light, map edges visible
panels.action: Akbar_jaimal_and_patta’s face fills the frame, eyes steady, jaw set, the glow of an oil lamp throwing shadows as his hand grips the map’s edge.

dialogue.speaker: Akbar_jaimal_and_patta
dialogue.text: If Mewar’s sword stays bare at our flank, how shall the empire rest?

i18n.hi: अगर मेवाड़ की तलवार हमारे पहलू पर नंगी रहे, तो सल्तनत चैन से कैसे सोए?

panels.shot: wide shot of Chittor’s defenders on the ramparts, Jaimal and Patta prominent among armoured Rajput nobles
panels.action: On the sunlit ramparts of Chittorgarh, Jaimal_jaimal_and_patta, a seasoned noble, stands in chain armour beside the younger Patta_jaimal_and_patta, both gripping spears as other Rajput warriors look out toward the plains.

dialogue.text: Rana Udai Singh withdrew to the hills; he left Chittor to trusted hands. The Akbarnama names Jaimal Rathor of Merta and the youth Patta of Kelwa among those who held the great fort in his stead.

i18n.hi: राणा उदय सिंह पहाड़ों को सरक गए; चित्तौड़ वो भरोसेमंदों के हवाले कर गए। अकबरनामा में मेरता के जैमल राठौड़ और केलवा के जवान पत्ता का नाम है, जो उनकी जगह क़िले पर डटे।

panels.shot: low-angle from Mughal trenches towards the towering walls, Akbar’s army arriving like a sea of troops and artillery
panels.action: Rows of Mughal matchlockmen and artillery pieces roll into shallow trenches facing the looming walls of Chittorgarh, with Akbar_jaimal_and_patta mounted in the middle distance overseeing the encampment.

dialogue.text: In October 1567, Akbar ringed Chittor with trenches, guns and earthworks. This was no quick raid, but a set siege meant to grind down stone, grain and resolve.

i18n.hi: अक़्तूबर १५६७ में अकबर ने खाइयों, तोपों और मिट्टी के बाँकों से चित्तौड़ को घेर लिया। ये कोई हल्की टक्कर नहीं, पत्थर, अनाज और हौसला सब को घिस डालने वाली घेराबंदी थी।

panels.shot: dynamic side view of Mughal sappers digging and pushing forward covered trenches under sporadic arrows from the walls
panels.action: Under a hazy sky, Mughal sappers bent over shovels push forward zigzag trenches protected by mantlets, while arrows arc down from the fort walls where Jaimal_jaimal_and_patta and other defenders oversee the archers.

dialogue.text: Abul Fazl describes trenches creeping ever closer, gabions inching forward under fire, mines sunk beneath bastions, and matchlocks cracking day after day against the stubborn stone of Chittor.

i18n.hi: अबुल फ़ज़्ल लिखता है कि खाइयाँ रेंगती हुई आगे बढ़ीं, गन्हों की दीवारें गोलियों के बीच धीरे-धीरे सिमटीं, बुर्जों के नीचे सुरंगें खोदी गईं, और बन्दूकें दिन-ब-दिन चित्तौड़ की ज़िद्दी दीवारों पर गरजीं।

panels.shot: medium of Akbar personally sighting a matchlock, with engineers gesturing toward a damaged bastion in the distance
panels.action: Akbar_jaimal_and_patta kneels behind a heavy matchlock set on a rest, peering along its barrel toward a distant bastion, while Mughal engineers point to a section of the wall already blackened and cracked by cannon fire.

dialogue.text: The emperor did not stay in a distant pavilion. The Akbarnama shows him in the trenches, directing fire, testing weapons, sharing the dust and danger of his men.

i18n.hi: बादशाह किसी दूर के शहनशाही शामियाने में नहीं था। अकबरनामा उसे खाइयों में दिखाता है—तोप चलवाते, हथियार आज़माते, सिपाहियों के साथ धूल और ख़तरा बाँटते।

panels.shot: tense night scene on the battlements, Jaimal on horseback within the fort, inspecting defenses by torchlight
panels.action: By torchlight on the inner side of the ramparts, Jaimal_jaimal_and_patta rides a horse along the wall-walk, conferring with sentries while distant flashes from Mughal guns light the night.

dialogue.speaker: Jaimal_jaimal_and_patta
dialogue.text: Hold through the night. Dawn will show which stone still stands.

i18n.hi: रात काट कर रखो। सवेरा बताएगा कौन सा पत्थर अब भी टिकता है।

panels.shot: dramatic medium shot framed from Akbar’s firing position, Jaimal on the wall in the distance, the matchlock centered
panels.action: Through the open fork of a matchlock rest, Jaimal_jaimal_and_patta is visible atop the wall, directing men; Akbar_jaimal_and_patta in the foreground steadies the gun, finger poised on the trigger.

dialogue.text: Then comes the moment Abul Fazl lingers on: he says Akbar himself took aim, fired from the trench, and struck Jaimal as the Rajput leader moved along the wall.

i18n.hi: फिर आता है वो पल जिस पर अबुल फ़ज़्ल ठहरता है: कहता है अकबर ने खुद निशाना साधा, खाई से गोली चलाई, और दीवार पर चलते हुए राजपूत सरदार जैमल को भेद दिया।

panels.shot: close-up on Jaimal reeling in the saddle, other defenders rushing to him as the wall behind shudders from impact
panels.action: Jaimal_jaimal_and_patta slumps in his saddle, clutching his side, as fellow defenders rush toward him along the battered wall, while dust and stone chips erupt from another cannon hit nearby.

dialogue.text: Badauni, writing outside the courtly panegyrics, echoes that Jaimal was felled and the defenders shaken, even as the wall itself reeled under shot and mine.

i18n.hi: दरबारी चाल से बाहर लिखने वाले बदायूँनी भी दोहराता है कि जैमल गिरा और रक्षक डगमगा गए, जबकि दीवारें भी तोप और सुरंग के धक्के से लड़खड़ा रही थीं।

panels.shot: wide, chaotic scene of a breached bastion, Mughal storming parties climbing while Rajput warriors resist desperately
panels.action: At a yawning breach in the wall, Mughal soldiers surge up ladders under a hail of arrows and stones, while Patta_jaimal_and_patta and other Rajput fighters stand in a tight knot, swords raised against the advancing line.

dialogue.text: With Jaimal wounded and bastions cracked, the Akbarnama tells of final assaults. The breach widened, ladders rose, and both chronicles speak of desperate hand-to-hand struggle on the broken stone.

i18n.hi: जैमल घायल और बुर्ज चटक चुके, अकबरनामा आख़िरी धावों की ख़बर देता है। शिगाफ़ चौड़ा हुआ, सीढ़ियाँ उठीं, और दोनों तवारीख़ टूटे पत्थर पर हाथों-हाथ की बेक़रार जंग लिखती हैं।

panels.shot: somber interior scene in Chittor, women gathered around a central courtyard where a firepit is being prepared
panels.action: Inside a stone courtyard, veiled women of various ages sit or stand in tense silence around a deep pit being filled with wood, their faces strained, as distant sounds of cannon echo through the fort.

dialogue.text: As the walls buckled, the Mughal court historian records another act. He writes that the women of Chittor performed jauhar, choosing death by fire rather than captivity in the stormed city.

i18n.hi: दीवारें झुकते ही मुग़ल दरबारी इतिहास एक और काम दर्ज करता है। वो लिखता है कि चित्तौड़ की औरतों ने जौहर किया—टूटते शहर में क़ैद से बेहतर आग में मरना चुना।

panels.shot: close, intimate shot of a woman’s hand placing bangles aside, other women silhouetted against the rising flames behind
panels.action: A close view shows a woman’s hand removing glass bangles and setting them gently on a stone ledge, while behind her other women stand in profile, their forms silhouetted by the growing light of unseen flames.

dialogue.text: No Mewar chronicle from that year survives to add their words. What we have is the victor’s Persian text, describing their act in the language of resolve and sacrifice as the fort’s last barrier fell.

i18n.hi: उस साल का कोई मेवाड़ी ब्यौरा नहीं बचा जो उनकी ज़बान जोड़ दे। हमारे पास फ़तह का फ़ारसी लेख है, जो क़िले की आख़िरी ढाल गिरते वक़्त उनके काम को जज़्बे और बलिदान की ज़बान में बयान करता है।

panels.shot: grim panoramic shot of Mughal troops pouring into the city streets below the fort, civilians fleeing in confusion
panels.action: From above, Mughal troops flood through a gate into the city streets, some houses burning, while men, women and children scatter in panic between narrow lanes and courtyards.

dialogue.text: Then the gates were forced. Akbar’s forces entered Chittor, and what followed is set down not by an enemy, but by his own historian, in words that still weigh on the memory of that day.

i18n.hi: फिर फाटक तोड़े गए। अकबर की फ़ौजें चित्तौड़ में घुसीं, और आगे जो हुआ उसे दुश्मन नहीं, उसके अपना इतिहासकार लिखता है—ऐसे लफ़्ज़ों में जो आज भी उस दिन की याद पर भारी हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot of Akbar on horseback inside the captured fort, expression hard, officers around him awaiting orders
panels.action: Akbar_jaimal_and_patta rides through a captured gate, his face grave, dust on his armour, as officers look to him in silence for direction amidst the smoke and rubble.

dialogue.text: According to the Akbarnama, the emperor ordered a general massacre of the captured residents. Abul Fazl speaks of a jihad against what he calls the ‘infidels’ of Chittor, framing the slaughter in religious war.

i18n.hi: अकबरनामा के मुताबिक़ बादशाह ने क़ैद किए बाशिंदों का आम क़त्लेआम हुक्म दिया। अबुल फ़ज़्ल इसे चित्तौड़ के ‘काफ़िरों’ पर जिहाद कहकर, उस नरसंहार को मज़हबी जंग की शक्ल देता है।

panels.shot: somber wide of bound men in groups under armed guards, with the ruined cityscape behind them
panels.action: Groups of unarmed Rajput and townsmen stand bound or surrounded by armed Mughal guards amid a ruined street, smoke drifting above broken houses and toppled gateways.

dialogue.text: Abul Fazl gives a number—thirty thousand Hindus put to death after the capture. Historians treat it as the Mughal court’s own claim, a figure to be weighed and examined, not erased or lightly dismissed.

i18n.hi: अबुल फ़ज़्ल एक आँकड़ा भी देता है—फ़तह के बाद तीस हज़ार हिन्दू मार डाले गए। इतिहासकार इसे खुद मुग़ल दरबार का दावा मानते हैं—तोलने और परखने का, मिटा देने या हल्के में उड़ा देने का नहीं।

panels.shot: close-up on Badauni at a writing desk, manuscript before him, as if reflecting uneasily
panels.action: Badauni_jaimal_and_patta, imagined as a bearded scholar, sits at a low desk with a manuscript, pausing with his reed pen above the page, his brow furrowed as if recalling the events he records.

dialogue.text: Badauni, no court flatterer, confirms the slaughter in his Muntakhab. He too speaks of the mass killing at Chittor, adding his voice to the Mughal record of what was done after the fort fell.

i18n.hi: दरबारी खुशामद से दूर बदायूँनी अपने मुन्तख़ब में इस क़त्लेआम की तसदीक करता है। वो भी चित्तौड़ में जन-समूह की हत्या लिखता है, क़िले के गिरने के बाद किए गए काम पर मुग़ल दस्तावेज़ में अपनी आवाज़ जोड़ता है।

panels.shot: quiet, desolate shot of Chittor’s devastated streets at dusk, a few survivors moving among blackened structures
panels.action: At dusk, Chittor’s inner streets lie in ruins, charred beams and collapsed walls casting long shadows, as a handful of exhausted survivors move slowly through the wreckage of homes and temples.

dialogue.text: The city that had seen earlier sacks now bore fresh scars. The fort stayed in Mughal hands, but the Sisodia line would nurse its loss and weave Chittor’s fall into the long song of Mewar’s defiance.

i18n.hi: जिस शहर ने पहले भी लूटें देखी थीं, अब नए ज़ख़्म ढोने लगा। क़िला मुग़लों के कब्ज़े में रहा, पर सिसोदिया वंश इस चोट को सँभालता रहा और चित्तौड़ की गिरावट को मेवाड़ की लंबी हुंकार में पिरोता गया।

panels.shot: transition shot showing Akbar later in life in a more reflective pose, court scene hinting at changed policies
panels.action: Years later in a calmer court, an older Akbar_jaimal_and_patta sits on a low throne in Agra, surrounded by Rajput nobles and scholars in varied dress, his face more contemplative than hard.

dialogue.text: Modern historians like Richards and Satish Chandra note that after such campaigns, Akbar’s Rajput policy deepened in alliance and accommodation, even as the memory of Chittor’s storm could not be unwritten.

i18n.hi: आधुनिक इतिहासकार, जैसे रिचर्ड्स और सतीश चंद्र, लिखते हैं कि ऐसी मुहिमों के बाद अकबर की राजपूत नीति और गहरी सुलह और साझेदारी की तरफ़ बढ़ी—भले चित्तौड़ के तूफ़ान की याद कभी मिट नहीं सकी।

panels.shot: medium shot inside Agra Fort courtyard, stone statues of Jaimal and Patta on war elephants being inspected by Akbar
panels.action: In the courtyard of Agra Fort, Akbar_jaimal_and_patta walks beside stone statues of Jaimal_jaimal_and_patta and Patta_jaimal_and_patta mounted on elephants, his gaze steady as artisans stand nearby awaiting his approval.

dialogue.text: The same Akbarnama that tells of jihad and massacre at Chittor also records an honor: Akbar ordered statues of Jaimal and Patta set up at Agra Fort, praising the courage of men he had fought and undone.

i18n.hi: यही अकबरनामा, जो चित्तौड़ पर जिहाद और क़त्लेआम लिखता है, एक इज़्ज़त भी दर्ज करता है: अकबर ने आगरा क़िले में जैमल और पत्ता की मूर्तियाँ लगवाईं—उन बहादुर दुश्मनों की दिलेरी को मान देते जिनसे लड़कर उन्हें गिराया।

panels.shot: close-up split composition: on one side Akbar’s face; on the other, a weathered stone of Chittor with faint carved figures
panels.action: The frame is split: on one side, a close view of Akbar_jaimal_and_patta’s thoughtful profile; on the other, a weathered Chittor wall where faint, almost ghostly carvings of warriors resemble Jaimal_jaimal_and_patta and Patta_jaimal_and_patta.

dialogue.text: In that single campaign, the record holds fury and tribute, faith and politics, imperial calculation and personal courage. It refuses to flatten the siege into an easy tale of villain and hero.

i18n.hi: एक ही मुहिम के लेखे में ग़ुस्सा भी है और सराहना भी, ईमान भी और सियासत भी, सल्तनती हिसाब-किताब भी और व्यक्तिगत दिलेरी भी। ये घेराबंदी को खलनायक-नायक की आसान कहानी में ढालने से इंकार करती है।

panels.shot: final wide of Chittorgarh today at sunrise, silent fort walls glowing, modern visitors tiny along the ramparts
panels.action: At sunrise in the present, Chittorgarh’s walls glow gold above quiet fields, a few small modern visitors walking along the ramparts, dwarfed by towers and ruined bastions that overlook the plains.

dialogue.text: To stand at Chittor today is to hear, behind every legend, the harder voice of the sources—Akbar, Jaimal and Patta bound together in a single siege, reminding us that honest memory does not seek to comfort.

i18n.hi: आज चित्तौड़ पर खड़े होना मतलब हर किवदंती के पीछे से उठती सख़्त आवाज़ें सुनना—अकबर, जैमल और पत्ता एक ही घेराबंदी में बंधे, याद दिलाते कि सच्ची याद सिर्फ़ दिलासा देने नहीं आती।

title_i18n.en: Chittorgarh and the Count of Thirty Thousand
title_i18n.hi: चित्तौड़ और तीस हज़ार की गिनती

subtitle_i18n.en: Akbar’s Fire at Chittor and the Count in the Victor’s Own Book
subtitle_i18n.hi: चित्तौड़ पर अकबर की आग और फ़तह के अपने लेखे में गिनती
